chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him).
Regarding a man who had sexual intercourse with a woman, if he maries her milk-mother or her daughter, he said, 'No' (it is forbidden).
And if a man has a wife and she commits fornication, he has the choice between keeping her or divorcing her, and divorce is not obligatory upon him for that.

key_terms.فَجَرَ: To commit fornication or have illicit sexual intercourse

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man marrying the milk-mother or daughter of a woman he had sexual relations with, and is divorce obligatory if she commits fornication?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the prohibition of marrying the milk-mother or daughter of the man who committed fornication with her is established as a definitive impediment. Furthermore, the Imam clarifies that while a wife's fornication grants her husband the discretion to divorce her, it does not impose an obligatory divorce (fara'j), distinguishing this ruling from cases where the impediment is permanent. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance between discretionary choice (ikhtiyar) and mandatory obligation (wujub) in marital dissolution.
